Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Rejoinder affidavit filed today in Court is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
No one has appeared for respondent no.2 despite notice.

3. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.234 of 2023, under Section 376, 452 IPC &
Section 5/6 of POCSO Act, P.S. Jagatpur, District Rae Bareli.
Shailendra vs State Of U.P. Thru.

1 4.

The FIR in question was lodged under Section 354, 452 IPC read with Section 7/8 of POCSO Act alleging that on 04.09.2023, the younger and elder daughters of the informant were alone at home;
the informant received a call at around 1 PM that the applicant has come at home.
When the parents came home and knocked on the door, they heard somebody running from the house.
It was also stated that the applicant was harassing the daughter of the informant for the last one year.
No allegation of rape was levelled in the FIR.
5. In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim disclosed her age as around 17 years and stated that she was in love with the applicant from the last one year.
It was also stated that the applicant came to the house and was lying with her and was touching inappropriately when suddenly, the sister of the victim woke up and called her parents.
When the parents came, the accused ran away.
It was specifically stated that no physical relations were formed in between them.
However, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the victim admitted that she knew the applicant from the last one year and used to like him.

With regard to the incident, for the first time,
it was stated that the applicant committed wrong on her.
In fact, she stated that she was raped on four occasions on the same night and when the parents came, the accused ran away.

6. The medical on record does not indicate any injury and the same was conducted on 07.09.2023 i.e. allegedly after three days of the alleged incident; and in fact, the FIR was also lodged on 06.09.2023.
7.

In the light of the said, learned counsel for the applicant states that the applicant may be enlarged on bail, particularly, when the applicant has no criminal antecedent and is in custody since 09.09.2023.
8.

Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that as per the High School certificate, the age of the victim is around 16 years 8 months as her date of birth is reflected as 12.01.2007, as such,
the bail application should be rejected.

9. Considering the submissions made, prima-facie, at the stage of statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., and in the FIR, no allegation of commission of offence under Section 376 IPC was made,
which was done for the first time in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

In view of the fact that in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., allegations of forming physical relations four times were made, and the same are not corroborated by the medical on record, thus, considering the variance in the statements which are not corroborated by the medical on record, the applicant who has no criminal antecedent and is in custody since 09.09.2023 is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant Shailendra be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
